summary: Modbus/TCP module is a T1-heavy safe-verify probe. Function 0x03 Read Holding Registers succeeds ONLY if a real Modbus stack answered — that plus device-ID (0x2B) and Report Slave ID (0x11) plus a bounded unit-ID sweep (2-15) gives strong evidence beyond a bare port scan. No T2 write proof (function 0x06/0x10) is ever sent — biggest gap is a safe canary WriteProperty (write to a scratch register the module then re-reads) which would upgrade the reachable finding from stance to proof-of-write.

findings.title_pattern: Modbus/TCP device on the scanned network
findings.tier_evidence: FC 0x03 response with valid MBAP + non-exception PDU is deterministic proof of a Modbus stack, not just port 502 open.
findings.promotion_notes: Add opt-in canary write: choose a holding register unused per config, FC 0x06 write a known sentinel (e.g., current value XOR 0xA5A5), FC 0x03 read it back, restore. Positive round-trip proves unauth write.
findings.tester_next_step: modpoll -m tcp -a 1 -r 1 -c 20 <ip>; for write proof (DESTRUCTIVE, do in test cell only): modpoll -m tcp -a 1 -r 100 -c 1 -t 4 <ip> 0x1234 && modpoll -m tcp -a 1 -r 100 -c 1 <ip>

findings.tier_evidence: Vendor/product/revision string via FC 0x2B — pure fingerprint, feeds CVE mapper.
findings.promotion_notes: Cross-reference vendor+product against Schneider/Siemens/AB advisories and emit a CVE-band finding (like s7._cve_fingerprint) at T1 when the identity positively matches a known-vulnerable family.
findings.tester_next_step: Feed vendor/product into a local CVE map (Schneider Modicon M340 / Siemens SIMATIC ET200 / AB MicroLogix defaults) and check hxxps://www.cisa.gov/news-events/ics-advisories; try default web UI creds admin/admin, admin/(blank), Administrator/Administrator on port 80/443 of the same host.

findings.tier_evidence: Multiple unit-IDs answering non-0x0B exceptions is deterministic proof of downstream serial slaves behind a gateway.
findings.promotion_notes: Follow the same canary-write path per downstream unit, gated behind --modbus-write. Also expand sweep to full 0-247 range under --modbus-full-sweep.
findings.tester_next_step: for u in $(seq 0 247); do modpoll -0 -1 -m tcp -a $u -r 1 -c 1 <ip>; done | grep -v 'Gateway Target'; each responding unit is a distinct PLC — attempt FC 0x11 Report Slave ID and FC 0x2B device-ID per unit.
